newsitem.title: FRANCE: Many French do not think ex-minister Hernu was spy.
newsitem.headline: Many French do not think ex-minister Hernu was spy.

text.p: Many French people do not believe that their former defence minister, the late Charles Hernu, once spied for the Soviet bloc, according to an opinion poll on Saturday.

The poll showed that a majority felt former president Francois Mitterrand acted wrongly in burying the case rather than investigating it when it was brought to his attention two years after the death in 1990 of Hernu, a personal friend.
Jacques Fournet, then chief of DST counter-intelligence, said this week that Warsaw Pact secret services told France four years ago about Hernu's alleged treason in the 1950s and 60s.
Hernu became Socialist defence minister in 1981-85 but nothing has been said about whether he was an agent while in office.

The poll, by the IFOP group for the weekly le Journal du Dimanche showed that 44 percent of the French did not believe information given by ex-Communist spies about Hernu compared to 36 percent who said they believed the purported disclosures.
Some 51 percent of the public said Mitterrand erred in ordering the case to be kept secret while 41 percent agreed with his decision to shield a dead comrade from dishonour.
The poll was conducted among 945 people between October 30-31.
